R7_quotes: Teach the Node project entry points `Program.fromProject` and `ingestProject` to honor the same `ProjectMeta.ingest` option.
justification: A lean, complete design. It has a tiny grammar (letters a–d, single ranges, star, at most four pieces), one Range kind for literals and classes, an exact 9x5 NFA row layout, a forward compile without patch lists, and a queue-based closure with dense sets. Its step budget (15,608) leaves headroom. The RegExp oracle uses anchored whole-text matching and is independent of the Typed code. Where infrastructure is missing it proposes the small changes: forwarding tape ingest in Node, and a `strings` list spec so pass checks see several NFA topologies. It does not design around them. There are no error codes, guards or extra profiles. Optimization value is good, though full pattern specialization has to wait for buffer bindings.

justification: Technically thorough and implementable. It correctly proposes the tape-ingest change. The widening, though, is deliberate: both kernels take their round/constant words as inputs and 'accept all bit patterns', and SHA handles two blocks (up to 119 bytes) although the doc says one block covers the core. The checks are spread across three extra cohorts (a standard-constants cohort per kernel and an ASCII cohort), and an IRWB-007 plan depends on immutable-buffer facts that do not exist. Loading K and the ChaCha constants from buffers also takes away the constant-propagation work the spec names. The rotates and register pressure remain.

justification: The strongest port design. It pins an upstream revision, reuses the source layout and helpers, and gives exact cell offsets for perft and search. It defines the two entries (with a small wrapper driving `chessSearchStep`) and drops upstream validation, clamping and overflow handling. It also proposes the missing `entries` metadata change. Probes measured real statement counts (9,206 for perft; 12,054–12,953 for search at budget 2), so the generated cases are sized against the gate from evidence. The oracle is the copied, independent chess.js reference data plus perft counts. The counted items are mostly faithful retention of upstream features: the node budget and the advanced-evaluation mode stay as inputs, and the budget-unwind path is tested. It also uses a fixed single board per entry as a workaround for `oneOf`'s scalar-only choice. Branchy search, ordering and extensions stay intact, giving the passes real work.

justification: A compact, exact LZ design. It has a one-byte tagged token over a 7-bit alphabet, frame-array heads/prev, a precise search/insert/emit order and a forward overlapping copy. R7_quotes: Choosing between two separate arrays would require a buffer-valued choice spec, since the current `oneOf` generator coerces its choice to an integer.

justification: A minimal, fully specified VM: nine opcodes, two-cell instructions, an integer if/else dispatch, and frame-array stack and locals. The complete 64-cell bytecode image is given and checks out (15n+4 and 13n+4 dispatches; 1,152 at n=12, seed=8). The step bound (11,904) and a JS reference VM give sizing and an independent oracle. A separate hand-specialized project stands in for specialization, which cannot bind buffer contents yet. It proposes the tape-ingest change. The only counted item is that it concatenates the two programs into one image with a scalar entry as a workaround for `oneOf`'s scalar-only choice. That is cheap, but it is still a workaround. The fixtures have no memory opcode, so sieve/sort-style memory traffic is absent. That slightly limits the bounds-check workload.

justification: Lean and well aimed. The FFT length is a scalar `n` in {8, 16}, so the existing specializer can bind it today, which directly serves the spec's specialization-constant point. It has a read-only twiddle table, a fixed stable two-band biquad with a small `dot3` inlining site, and a binary64 DFT/direct-recurrence oracle with an RMS dB bound. Small estimates (under 5,000 and under 2,500 statements) sit well within the gate. The only extra configuration is the narrowed n=16 case spec from the scalar specialization step. The table cells are given as placeholders, but the doc says exactly how to compute and pack them. It proposes the reference-runner signature fix instead of working around it. Nothing an implementer would cut.

Neither weighs much. It exercises dispatch, code/stack/data bounds checks and register-resident VM state well.

R8_quotes: Run the same checked pipeline with profiles for empty, `ab`, `a|bc|d`, `a?a?`, `a*b` and `a?a?a?a?|a*a*|[a-c]*[a-c]*`.
100 generated cases per profile for seeds 7 and 23
justification: A workable but heavier regex design. It supports a broader grammar (alternation of up to three branches, `?` and `*`, a–z, at most eight atoms) with a right-to-left Thompson compiler and four state kinds. The compiler is described clearly enough, though alternation merging takes care to get right. It widens the text domain to all ASCII including NUL and newline, which needs a lookahead-based RegExp oracle. Because `oneOf` cannot choose strings, it designs around this with six extra fixed-pattern profiles run as separate Programs, plus an exhaustive sweep. It also gives a paragraph to future specialization experiments the doc says cannot run yet. The planning budget of 18,680 against the 20,000 gate leaves little headroom. The oracle is independent and the dispatch, range-test and closure work gives the passes real targets.
